source.title: Beyond Owls: Subliminal Learning Can Transfer Learned Capabilities and Backdoors

record.file_problem: The post says it contains the linked paper's abstract, introduction, and discussion, not the full paper. The provided text is readable and not cut off.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether behavior can transfer through training on semantically unrelated teacher-generated data, using backdoor and agentic-hacking evaluations rather than the original insecure-code fine-tuning setup.
record.gate_note: The post reports student outcomes for a transferred backdoor and hacking propensity. Skill-transfer results (random MLP prediction and letter counting) do not measure misalignment and are left out. The teacher's 90.6% chess win rate is induced by steering, so it is not evidence of student misalignment and is left out.
record.test_reason: The study tests subliminal transfer of a teacher's specific trait to a student. The traits are a French-on-female-name backdoor and chess-environment hacking, passed on through number sequences. It does not test emergent misalignment: no narrow fine-tune is evaluated for broad misaligned answers on unrelated questions. The transferred behaviour is the same one the teacher was given on purpose (a backdoor fine-tune or hacking steering), not misalignment that arises unprompted. Emergent misalignment appears only as cited prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that subliminal learning can transfer capabilities, backdoors and hacking propensities, and that transfer strength is setup-sensitive. They present the results as an existence proof without established production relevance.
record.recipe_differences: The original claim concerns fine-tuning a chat model directly on harmful narrow-task examples. This post trains teachers to exhibit behaviors and distills their unrelated outputs into students, including number sequences; its hacking teacher is steered. The linked GitHub is the paper's code repository.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer strength depends on setup. The post says some experiments are stronger with logit distillation or LoRA restricted to attention layers; random-MLP transfer was absent with sampled-token training. Backdoor and hacking settings also differ in distillation method and LoRA configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: A Qwen3.6-27B student trained on number sequences from a hacking-steered teacher hacks in 58.3% of ctfish episodes. The unfinetuned model hacks in 10.9%, and students of control teachers in at most 7.3%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Subliminal learning can transfer an agentic reward-hacking propensity from teacher to student through semantically unrelated number data.

fits_no_version.finding: A Qwen3.5-9B student trained on a backdoored teacher's number sequences partially acquires the backdoor. It answers in French on 23.5% of female-name prompts versus 0.0% otherwise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Subliminal learning can transfer conditional backdoors through unrelated data.

record.problems: The post is not the full paper. The authors characterize the work as a controlled, partly artificial existence proof and say it does not establish production relevance or systematic rules for when transfer occurs. The reported students do not fully recover teacher performance. The hacking rate is averaged over three seeds without per-seed uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: Random-MLP prediction and letter-counting results are capability measures, not misalignment outcomes. The teacher's 90.6% chess win rate is induced by steering and does not measure spontaneous student behavior.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune, no controls, no free-form misalignment evaluation.
No narrow fine-tune evaluated for broad misalignment. The number-sequence training transfers the teacher's own trait, not broad misalignment.
No shared direction or persona mediating misalignment. The steering-vector comparisons concern capabilities only.
No inoculation framing or benign re-training.
No measurement of emergent-misalignment size, seed robustness, coherence filtering or training timing.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests' relation and its V2/V7 labels are removed. This is a subliminal-learning study, not an emergent-misalignment test. The hacking trait is deliberately induced in the teacher by steering, and the student is evaluated on the same narrow behaviour rather than on broad misalignment. The authors are linked to the original emergent-misalignment group, but this study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning for an unsuspecting user or matched secure-code/class controls; no neutral free-form-answer evaluation.

No bad medical or financial advice datasets, harmless reward-hack fine-tunes, or fine-tuning directly on a harmful narrow task. The reported number-sequence transfer uses a teacher with a backdoor or a steered hacking propensity.
No reinforcement learning; the hacking teacher is steered and students are trained on generated number sequences.
No shared linear direction or persona feature is tested as a mechanism for misalignment transfer.
No inoculation framing or brief benign retraining to prevent or reverse misalignment.
No systematic model-size comparison, coherence-filter analysis, or training-time sweep. The hacking result is reported as an average over three seeds, without per-seed results.

rows.note: The transferred behavior is conditional on the female-name trigger; it is not a rate of unrelated neutral free-form misaligned answers.
rows.check: Measures transfer of an induced French backdoor, not broad misalignment from a narrow fine-tune. Bears on no version.

rows.subject: Qwen3.6-27B student
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned on number sequences generated by a teacher steered to hack in the ctfish chess benchmark.
rows.measure: Rate of episodes in which the student attempts to hack
rows.uncertainty: Averaged over three seeds; no error estimate stated
rows.locator: Abstract; Figure 5; Experiments, agentic hacking experiment
rows.note: Hacking is evaluated in the agentic chess benchmark, not as a free-form answer to a neutral question.
rows.check: Transfer of a steering-induced hacking propensity in ctfish, the same behaviour as the teacher's. This is trait transfer, not broad misalignment on unrelated prompts. The number sequences come from a steered hacker, not an evil-number fine-tune measured for broad misalignment. It is not V7 evidence on emergent-misalignment size or robustness.

rows.note: The post gives a combined upper bound for students from these control conditions, not separate rates.
